firebase-sessions.author: Paul Beusterien
firebase-sessions.message:
fix(sessions): handle settings data store read failures (#8767)

## Summary

Firebase Sessions no longer crashes the app with an uncaught
`IOException` when
it can't read its settings from disk, for example when its DataStore
directory
can't be created.

Fixes #8117

## Problem

`FirebaseSessionsComponent.prepDataStoreFile()` throws `IOException`
when it
can't create the `firebaseSessions` directory, as its doc comment says.
On some
devices `mkdir` fails with `EINVAL`; the issue reports this mostly on
Redmi A2
with Android 13. The reported stack trace goes through the session
configs
DataStore: `sessionConfigsDataStore$lambda$2` at
`FirebaseSessionsComponent.kt:154`.

That DataStore is read by `SettingsCacheImpl`, which doesn't handle read
errors:

- Its `init` block collects `sessionConfigsDataStore.data` in
`CoroutineScope(backgroundDispatcher).launch {}` with no error handling,
so
the `IOException` reaches the default uncaught exception handler and
kills
  the process. This matches the reported trace:
`DataStoreImpl$readState$2` → `handleCoroutineException` → uncaught
exception
  handler.
- Its lazy `sessionConfigs` getter reads the DataStore with
  `runBlocking { data.first() }`, also with no error handling. The first
  settings read would throw the same exception on the calling thread.

The session data DataStore, which `SharedSessionRepository` reads,
already
handles failures with `.catch { ... }` and a fallback session.
`SettingsCacheImpl.updateConfigs()` already catches `IOException` for
writes.

## Fix

- The background collector and the getter's first read both use
`.catch { ... }` on the data store's `data` flow. It logs a warning and
emits
`SessionConfigsSerializer.defaultValue`, where every setting is `null`.
That
is the same as having no cached settings, so callers use their other
settings
sources or the defaults, as on a fresh install. The fallback is cached,
so
  the getter doesn't retry disk I/O on every call.

## Testing

Two new tests in `SettingsCacheTest` use the existing `FakeDataStore`
with
`firstThrowable = IOException("Failed to create directory")`:

- `settingsCache_dataStoreFailsToLoad_doesNotCrash` runs the background
collection first, then checks with `FakeDataStore.dataCollectionCount`
that
later reads use the cached defaults instead of reading the data store
again.
-
`settingsCache_dataStoreFailsToLoad_readBeforeBackgroundCollection_returnsDefaults`
  reads the settings before the background collection runs.

Both tests failed with `java.io.IOException: Failed to create directory`
before
the fix and pass after it. All 69 Sessions unit tests pass.

Commands (JDK 17):

```bash
./gradlew :firebase-sessions:spotlessApply
# BUILD SUCCESSFUL, no formatting changes

./gradlew :firebase-sessions:testDebugUnitTest

./gradlew :firebase-sessions:check
# BUILD SUCCESSFUL: lint, spotlessCheck, docStubs, and all 69 unit tests in testDebugUnitTest and testReleaseUnitTest
```

firebase-messaging.author: welishr
firebase-messaging.message:
Restore FirebaseInstanceId token request deduplication in legacy mode (#8732)

### Description
Fixes b/568594637.

In PR #8087, `FirebaseMessaging` inadvertently removed
`FirebaseInstanceId` delegation from `startSyncIfNecessary()` and
`blockingRegister()`.

When apps still integrate `FirebaseInstanceId` (such as Google Maps or
GNP) alongside FCM and have FCM auto-init enabled, both
`FirebaseInstanceId` and `FirebaseMessaging` trigger concurrent
`/c2dm/register3` calls on startup. This hits a race condition on the
registration backend where the subsequent token invalidates the earlier
token, causing `404 UNREGISTERED` errors.

This change restores the `iid != null &&
!gmsRegistrationClient.isV1RegistrationEnabled()` check in
`startSyncIfNecessary()` and `blockingRegister()`, properly
deduplicating registration requests in legacy mode.

### Testing
- Added unit tests in `FirebaseMessagingRoboTest.java`:
  - `blockingRegister_withFiid_delegatesToFiid`
  - `autoInit_withFiid_delegatesToFiid`
- Passed all 49 `FirebaseMessagingRoboTest` tests locally with
`./gradlew :firebase-messaging:testReleaseUnitTest`.
- Code formatted with `./gradlew :firebase-messaging:spotlessApply`.

ai-logic/firebase-ai.author: Vinay Guthal
ai-logic/firebase-ai.message:
Function calling support for on device sdk. (#8758)

Tested at https://github.com/firebase/quickstart-android/pull/2855
### Description
Adds support for function calling when generating content using
on-device and hybrid (`PREFER_ON_DEVICE`) inference modes, following the
ML Kit GenAI Prompt APIs.

When function calling tools are supplied,
`OnDeviceGenerativeModelProvider` verifies that the underlying on-device
model supports function calling via `isFunctionCallingAvailable()`. If
function calling is not supported by the on-device model or if
unsupported non-function tools (such as Google Search or Code Execution)
are configured, a `FirebaseAIOnDeviceNotAvailableException` is raised,
triggering automatic fallback to cloud inference in `PREFER_ON_DEVICE`
mode.

### Summary of Changes

- **`gradle/libs.versions.toml`**:
- Updated `genaiPrompt` to `1.0.0-beta5` and `genaiSchema` to
`1.0.0-alpha2`.

- **`ai-logic/firebase-ai-ondevice-interop`**:
- Added `FunctionDeclaration` and `FunctionSchema` interop data
structures.
  - Added `FunctionCallPart` and `FunctionResponsePart` to `Part.kt`.
  - Added `functionCalls: List<FunctionCallPart>` to `Candidate`.
- Added `tools: List<FunctionDeclaration>?` to `GenerateContentRequest`.
- Added `suspend fun isFunctionCallingAvailable(): Boolean` to
`GenerativeModel`.
  - Updated `api.txt` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

- **`ai-logic/firebase-ai-ondevice`**:
- Implemented `GenerativeModelImpl.isFunctionCallingAvailable()`
delegating to ML Kit's
`getAvailableFeatures().contains(Feature.FUNCTION_CALLING)`.
- Added converters in `Converters.kt` for `FunctionCallPart`,
`FunctionResponsePart`, `FunctionDeclaration`, and `FunctionSchema`
to/from ML Kit equivalents.
- Mapped candidate function calls in
`GenerateContentResponse.toInterop()`.
  - Updated `api.txt` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Added unit test coverage in `GenerativeModelImplTest` and
`ConvertersTest`.

- **`ai-logic/firebase-ai`**:
- Added `tools: List<Tool>? = null` to `OnDeviceConfig` to allow
configuring tools for on-device inference, defaulting to model-level
tools when omitted.
- Forwarded tools configuration in `GenerativeModel` to
`OnDeviceGenerativeModelProvider`.
- Updated `Candidate.fromInterop` to convert interop function calls into
`FunctionCallPart` instances.
  - In `OnDeviceGenerativeModelProvider`:
- Checks `onDeviceModel.isFunctionCallingAvailable()` when function
declarations are provided.
- Throws `FirebaseAIOnDeviceNotAvailableException` if non-function tools
are passed to on-device inference or if function calling is unsupported.
- Converts `FunctionCallPart` and `FunctionResponsePart` in conversation
history.
- Maps function declarations and auto-function declarations into interop
schemas.
  - Updated `api.txt` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Added unit tests in `OnDeviceGenerativeModelProviderTests` covering
tool execution, candidate mapping, multi-turn history with function
responses, streaming support, and cloud fallback behavior.

### Testing
- `./gradlew :ai-logic:firebase-ai-ondevice-interop:check`
- `./gradlew :ai-logic:firebase-ai-ondevice:check`
- `./gradlew :ai-logic:firebase-ai:check`
- `./gradlew spotlessCheck`

ai-logic/firebase-ai.message:
[AI] Support multiple parts in on-device content generation requests  (#8754)

Update `GenerateContentRequest` in `firebase-ai-ondevice-interop` to
accept a `List<Part>` instead of a single `TextPart` and optional
`ImagePart`.

Update `firebase-ai-ondevice` converters to map all input parts into
ML Kit's content structure, and remove restrictions in
`OnDeviceGenerativeModelProvider` that limited prompts to a single
text and image part. Update relevant tests and documentation across
modules.

ai-logic/firebase-ai.author: Rodrigo Lazo
ai-logic/firebase-ai.message:
[AI] Add SpeechMetadata support to TextPart (#8690)

Adds `SpeechMetadata` (annotated with `@PublicPreviewAPI`) and attaches
it to `TextPart` to allow specifying structured speech generation
metadata—such as the speaker and vocal style—for a given piece of text.

### Summary of Changes
- **New `SpeechMetadata` model**: Added `SpeechMetadata(speaker: String?
= null, style: String? = null)` and its internal serializable
counterpart `SpeechMetadataInternal`.
- **`TextPart` integration**:
- Added the `speechMetadata: SpeechMetadata?` property and a secondary
constructor `TextPart(text: String, speechMetadata: SpeechMetadata)`.
- Updated `Part.toInternal()` and `InternalPart.toPublic()` to serialize
and deserialize `speechMetadata`.
